activity_summary: You asked your father straight, before church, why he would not come. He said the bailiff's man stood at the porch with paper. You told him the paper was lighter. He blamed a fairy and refused the thanks. He did not come. Susanna asked whether it was paid or only promised. You did not say by whom. The sword stayed on the nail.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Asked once, refused the errand to the porch, and did not name the shops.

entities.name: John Shakespeare
entities.context: Stayed in the shop, blamed a fairy, and shut his own door.

entities.name: Mary Shakespeare
entities.context: Cut the story short, sent the dry gloves up, and made him eat.

entities.name: Anne Shakespeare
entities.context: Took the house to church and kept the sword off the lane.

entities.name: Joan Shakespeare
entities.context: Took Judith's hand and brushed the ink off his cuff.

entities.name: Susanna Shakespeare
entities.context: Asked whether the paper was paid or only promised.

entities.name: Judith Shakespeare
entities.context: Applied his rule about thanking, and asked whether the sword could go as far as the lane.

entities.name: Hamnet Shakespeare
entities.context: Heard from the shop side. The sword stayed on the nail.

facets.activity: Asked Father why he stayed home from church

quotes.speaker: john_shakespeare
quotes.text: I don't go because Master Bailiff's man stands at the porch with paper, and I've no wish to read it.

quotes.speaker: john_shakespeare
quotes.text: Then some fairy's been at my reckoning. I'll not thank a fairy. It spoils them.

quotes.speaker: william_shakespeare
quotes.text: The paper's lighter than it was, Father.

quotes.speaker: susanna_shakespeare
quotes.text: Was it paid, or did a gentleman say it would be?
